title: Life Agent MVP mobile sync wire contracts
description: Closed v1 contracts for push, per-operation ACK/error, frozen bootstrap and incremental pull. This schema and the HTTP manifest are the normative implementation source; the repository validator is acceptance evidence only. The M2 endpoint parser accepts only the recursive rawJsonValue subset before hashing: null, booleans, strings, interoperable safe integers, bounded arrays and objects with schema-safe ASCII keys. Floating-point tokens, exponent notation, unsafe integers, duplicate keys, excessive nesting and excessive total nodes fail closed before canonicalization.

canonicalUtcInstant.description: Canonical UTC instant with uppercase T/Z, mandatory seconds and either no fractional part or exactly three fractional digits. Calendar validity is enforced by the date-time format checker.

cursor.description: Canonical unpadded base64url opaque random handle only, with at least 43 characters so generation 1 carries at least 256 bits of server-generated entropy. Server-side lookup binds generation 1 of the handle to the derived person, receiving device, credential family, protocol stream, bootstrap_id/snapshot when applicable, exact position, expiry, signing-key generation and purge generation. The client never parses or guesses a cursor. Expiry has one endpoint-specific outcome: an expired bootstrap next-page snapshot returns cursor_expired with HTTP 410; an expired incremental snapshot or unavailable retained history returns bootstrap_required with HTTP 409. sync_pull never returns cursor_expired. Account deletion and privacy purge invalidate and delete every bound handle.

rawJsonValue.description: Closed recursive M2 ingress value. The transport parser additionally enforces maximum nesting depth 32 and maximum 10000 total value nodes before hashing, with a safe request_schema_invalid failure on every limit or canonicalization error.

device_id.description: Pending operation identity remains enrollment-independent. Room v3 stores a separate deterministic wire materialization; any M1 legacy local operation bytes/hash are not the M2 wire digest. The submitting device is derived only from the authenticated top-level device binding.

pushOperation.description: After strict schema validation and physical ordinal equality, normative semantic consistency is checked before operation_content_sha256: wrapper operation/capture/event/revision/schema identifiers equal their nested capture and body identifiers; capture and body identity, source, origin, collector, recorded_at and note payload agree; capture integrity is SHA-256 and byte length of RFC 8785/JCS capture.content. revision.content_sha256 is SHA-256 of the RFC 8785/JCS object with exactly these keys and values: event_id=body.event_id, revision_id=body.revision_id, revision_no=body.revision_no, capture_id=body.source.capture_id, operation_id=body.source.operation_id, record_status=body.record_status, effective_time=body.time, recorded_at=body.source.recorded_at, payload=body.payload, correction_reason=body.revision.correction_reason, parent_revision_id=null for a root or the sole body.revision.parents[0].revision_id. Any such consistency failure is schema_invalid. Parent lineage or revision_no other than root 1 / parent + 1 is invalid_parent. Only after these stages are operation hash, ownership, immutable registries, dependency resolution and CAS evaluated.

ordinal.description: Must equal this operation's zero-based physical index in the raw operations array. A schema-valid item with another ordinal receives schema_invalid while later items continue.

client_sequence.description: Stable installation-scoped outbox sequence. It does not change when an unacknowledged operation is moved to a new batch. Before dependency resolution the server claims (installation_id, client_sequence) -> (operation_id, operation_content_sha256) immutably. An exact tuple with a prior retryable missing_parent may be re-evaluated in a later batch; changing operation_id or digest returns client_sequence_collision. Terminal prior outcomes remain stable.

operation_id.description: Claimed with its operation_content_sha256 before dependency resolution. A retryable missing_parent keeps this immutable claim: exact unchanged bytes may be re-evaluated later, changed digest is operation_id_collision, and a second physical occurrence in the same first-seen batch is operation_id_collision.

capture_id.description: Claimed for this operation before dependency resolution; another operation cannot reuse it while a missing_parent retry remains pending.

event_id.description: An existing event_id may be reused by an authorized valid descendant revision in its rooted lineage, including a stale descendant that receives a conflict ACK. Immutable event ownership is the server-derived person plus event_id, event kind and root lineage. installation_id, local_owner_id and device_id are per-revision provenance and MAY differ for an authorized descendant submitted from a replacement device. Reusing event_id under another person, with an incompatible kind or root lineage, or submitting a second root with expected_current_revision_id null for an existing event returns event_id_collision.

revision_id.description: Claimed for this operation before dependency resolution; another operation cannot reuse it while a missing_parent retry remains pending.

expected_current_revision_id.description: Compare-and-set pointer: null for a root revision or the sole superseded parent for a linear M2 note revision. Two-parent conflict resolution is not part of the M2 notes wire subset.

operation_content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785/JCS serialization of this complete push operation with only ordinal and operation_content_sha256 omitted. It binds stable sequence, CAS expectation, wrapper semantics, capture and event while allowing the same operation to move to another batch ordinal. The server claims operation_id plus this digest before dependency resolution. An exact terminal receipt committed before the batch is replayed; an exact prior retryable missing_parent is re-evaluated; any changed digest is operation_id_collision. A second physical occurrence inside one first-seen batch is operation_id_collision even with the same digest.

batch_id.description: HTTP Idempotency-Key must equal this durable push identity. Durable replay uses a protected fingerprint of the exact raw HTTP request BODY bytes in the endpoint replay namespace; it is intentionally separate from batch_content_sha256.

batch_content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785/JCS serialization of the successfully parsed closed-subset envelope with only batch_content_sha256 omitted. It is validated before any operation item is dereferenced or strictly validated. It is not the durable raw-byte replay fingerprint.

operations.description: The closed envelope deliberately retains raw subset array items. After duplicate-key, lexical-number, body-size, nesting/node-limit and envelope-hash checks, each item is validated independently against pushOperation in physical array order. One malformed item therefore receives an indexed error without suppressing valid items after it.

batch_id.description: HTTP Idempotency-Key MUST equal this durable push identity. Exact batch_id plus the same fingerprint of the exact raw HTTP request BODY bytes returns the byte-identical frozen response BODY. Any raw BODY byte difference, including whitespace or object-member order, with the same ID produces batch_id_collision before processing. Authorization header rotation is outside this fingerprint.

device_id.description: Must equal the server-side device binding of the opaque authenticated access token. It is not accepted as ownership by itself.

batch_content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785/JCS serialization of the successfully parsed closed-subset request with only batch_content_sha256 omitted. This canonical parsed-value digest is distinct from the exact raw HTTP BODY replay fingerprint and is checked before per-operation dereference or semantic validation.

operations.description: For per-operation errors, ingress validates the closed raw batch envelope and its batch hash first, then validates each raw array item independently against pushOperation. Pending/new accepted operations must match the submitting session's device and installation/local-owner enrollment binding; person ownership is derived only from the access token. Historical bootstrap and pull records preserve their original submitting provenance and are not rebound to a receiving replacement device.

path.description: Tiny schema-owned location set: the request root or one physical operations index from 0 through 99. Attacker-controlled property names and deeper paths are never reflected.

operationAck.description: Durable terminal operation receipt. When bootstrap or pull later delivers the same operation_id, Android performs insert-or-verify against operation_id, operation_content_sha256, result_code, capture_id, event_id, revision_id, current_revision_id, server_sequence and committed_at (the latter equals serverChange.event.server.received_at). An exact match is a no-op that creates no duplicate and rewrites no receipt; any mismatch is an integrity failure that halts sync for explicit recovery.

replayed.description: False remains frozen on an exact same-batch replay. True only when this operation was already committed in a different first-seen batch before the current batch was processed.

current_revision_id.description: The exact event head observed by the server after this terminal outcome. A conflict receipt may reference a head not yet present locally; the durable receipt is stored without requiring a local revision foreign key and a later pull fills the historical record.

ordinal.description: The current response item's physical request-array index. A cross-batch replay of an exact terminal invalid_parent operation regenerates this ordinal for its new physical position; ordinal is not part of the stable terminal item receipt projection.

operation_id.description: Null only when the raw item had no syntactically valid operation_id.

error_code.description: First-match-wins per-item precedence after the raw envelope succeeds: (1) safely inspect only string discriminators in order event_schema_version, operation_kind, event_kind and capture/body source channel; (2) validate strict pushOperation schema; (3) require ordinal equal physical array index; (4) require the normative wrapper/capture/body identity, source, payload, capture-integrity and immutable-revision consistency defined by pushOperation; failures in stages 2-4 are schema_invalid; (5) verify operation_content_sha256, otherwise operation_hash_mismatch; (6) verify authenticated ownership, otherwise ownership_violation; (7) consult and claim immutable registries in order operation_id, installation-scoped client_sequence, capture_id, revision_id and event_id; (8) persist operation_id, client_sequence, capture_id and revision_id claims before resolving the parent and root/parent+1 revision_no, returning missing_parent only for an absent parent and invalid_parent for lineage or revision-number failure; (9) compare expected_current_revision_id with current_by_event. The persisted claims survive both dependency outcomes. Exact unchanged missing_parent may be re-evaluated in a later batch. invalid_parent is a frozen terminal item outcome with field_errors exactly empty; on an exact cross-batch replay only ordinal is regenerated for the operation's current physical index, while operation_id, operation_content_sha256, status, error_code, retryable and field_errors remain the stable receipt projection. Changed content requires a new operation identity. A second physical occurrence of operation_id in one first-seen batch is operation_id_collision. CAS mismatch emits a terminal conflict ACK. Only the earliest failure is evaluated.

retryable.description: Only missing_parent is retryable. Dependency resolution occurs after immutable operation_id, client_sequence, capture_id and revision_id claims are persisted. For missing_parent, only the exact unchanged operation may be submitted in a later batch and re-evaluated after the parent arrives. invalid_parent retains the same claims but is terminal; an exact cross-batch replay returns the stable terminal error with field_errors empty and ordinal regenerated to the current physical index. Every nonretryable item error is terminal for those exact operation bytes and is not automatically resubmitted; an explicit data change requires a new operation identity/digest.

field_errors.description: At most eight controlled entries per item keeps a 100-result response below the 512 KiB transport cap. Unknown raw property names are never copied into paths. invalid_parent requires exactly an empty array so its stable terminal receipt has no path tied to a prior batch ordinal.

pushBatchResponse.description: Frozen response for a first-seen batch. An exact same-batch retry returns byte-identical bytes, including replayed and server_time.

results.description: Exactly one result is returned for every raw request operation, in request-array order. Cross-message cardinality and ordinal equality are mandatory semantic checks.

server_high_watermark.description: Informational server cursor hint after committed ACKs. It does not replace the client's applied pull cursor.

serverChange.description: Immutable historical delivery record derived from the accepted pending pushOperation with only these enrichments: capture.persistence_state changes local_pending to authenticated_ingress; capture.identity.device_id changes null to the authenticated submitting device_id; event.persistence_state changes local_pending to server_committed; event.identity.device_id changes null to that same submitting device_id; event.server.received_at and event.server.server_sequence change from null to the exact ACK committed_at and server_sequence. Every other capture/event field is byte-for-byte JSON-value equivalent to the accepted operation. Historical installation, local owner and submitting device provenance need not equal the top-level receiving device of a later bootstrap or pull page. If Android already stores an ACK for operation_id, applying this change is insert-or-verify: operation_id, operation_content_sha256, result_code, capture_id, event_id, revision_id, current_revision_id, server_sequence and event.server.received_at/ACK committed_at must match exactly. A match is a no-op without duplicate insertion or receipt rewrite; a mismatch halts sync as an integrity failure.

current_revision_id.description: State-machine head after this sequence. For applied, expected_current_revision_id equaled the prior head and this revision becomes current. For stale compare-and-set conflict, this is exactly the unchanged prior head and the conflicting revision is retained only as history.

operation_content_sha256.description: Digest of the originally accepted pending push operation. It is not recomputed from the enriched committed documents.

request_id.description: Durable page replay identity. The same request_id with byte-identical request bytes returns the byte-identical cached page; changed bytes produce request_id_collision.

bootstrap_id.description: Client-generated identifier retained for every page of one explicit restore attempt.

page_cursor.description: Null for the first page; otherwise the exact authenticated next_page_cursor from the preceding page.

bootstrapResponse.description: Frozen page of an explicit restore snapshot. Bootstrap into a nonempty Android database is staged across all pages and, only after final validation, atomically replaces the server-committed/authenticated-ingress partition. It preserves local_pending captures/events, durable outbox operations and terminal receipts; reconciliation of any overlapping operation_id follows insert-or-verify and never silently rewrites an ACK.

request_id.description: Exact echo of the durable bootstrap request identity.

from_page_cursor.description: Exact echo of the request page_cursor. It prevents a valid page from another bootstrap position being applied to this request.

page_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the RFC 8785/JCS serialization of this complete response with only page_sha256 omitted. All other fields, including server_time, are frozen for an exact page replay.

changes.description: Globally unique, strictly increasing and topologically ordered snapshot prefix, bounded by the corresponding request page_size. Every parent appears earlier in the stream, including across page boundaries. Applied revisions advance current_by_event; conflicts preserve exactly the prior event head. Historical nested provenance remains tied to the original submitting device and need not match this response's receiving device.

incremental_cursor.description: Frozen high-watermark cursor shared by all pages and persisted only with the final page.

request_id.description: Durable page replay identity. The same request_id with byte-identical request bytes returns the byte-identical cached page; changed bytes produce request_id_collision.

pullResponse.description: Validated changes and next_cursor commit atomically. Before applying any overlapping operation_id, Android insert-or-verifies the retained terminal ACK against operation digest, result, current head, server sequence and committed/received time. Exact overlap is a no-op; any drift aborts the entire page and cursor transaction as protocol integrity failure.

request_id.description: Exact echo of the durable pull request identity.

page_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the RFC 8785/JCS serialization of this complete response with only page_sha256 omitted. All other fields, including server_time, are frozen for an exact page replay.

changes.description: Globally unique, strictly increasing, topologically ordered continuation after from_cursor and across every page. Every parent exists earlier in the combined bootstrap/pull stream. Applied revisions advance current_by_event; conflicts preserve exactly the prior event head. Historical nested provenance remains tied to the original submitting device and need not match this response's receiving device.
